title: Mars Bar from 1991 found – and it's 20g bigger than today's
titleZh: 1991 年发现的 Mars Bar，比现在的大 20 克
author: RickJWagner
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Mars Bar from 1991 found – and it's 56% bigger than today's8 hours agoEleanor MaslinEast Yorkshire and LincolnshireVictoria GordonNow and then... the 1991 Mars Bar alongside one from todayA 35-year-old Mars Bar has been found during a house clearance – and the discovery has gone viral amid claims it highlights the effect of "shrinkflation".The chocolate bar with a best-before date of 1991 was found during a clear-out of a house in Scunthorpe.Victoria Gordon, who runs the cleaning service, posted a photo on social media of the 62.5g bar alongside one of today's Mars Bars, which is 40g."It was nearly as big as my hand, which was kind of why I noticed it," she said.Victoria GordonVictoria Gordon found the old Mars Bar on 5 AugustSpeaking on BBC Radio Lincolnshire, Gordon said: "We were clearing out a hoarder's house and everything we were rooting through was decades old."This Mars Bar stood out to me because as I picked it up it was nearly the whole length of my hand."I was like, 'Wow, look at the size of that!'"Who makes Mars Bars?Mars Bars are made by US company Mars, Incorporated.The manufacturer also owns several other chocolate brands including Celebrations chocolate tubs, Galaxy, Hotel Chocolat, M&Ms and Maltesers.It also owns non-chocolate brands including Dreamies, Hubba Bubba, Pedigree and Whiskas.The company was founded in 1883 by Frank C Mars, from Minnesota, with his mother Elva teaching him how to hand-dip chocolate.A Mars spokesperson said: "Over the last 35 years, we have made a number of updates to our bar sizes and pack formats to reflect consumer demand, alongside considering wider external factors such as manufacturing costs and the price of cocoa."SuppliedThe chocolate was found during a house clearanceGordon, who runs Pocket Rockets, is not sure what she will do with the bar, but she said she might be sitting on a "gold mine"."I do post some hoarding videos but I've never had anything go this viral," she said."It's so fascinating what people find so interesting. I almost put it in the skip [but] I might do a UK tour with it."Related storiesRelated internet links

comments.author: smolder
comments.textRawHtml: Shrinkflation is all over. Burger buns at fast food places were more dense 20 years ago. The small burgers had 1/8th pound patties instead of the current 1/10th pound. It's hard to find a product that hasn't gotten worse or more expensive, even adjusted for inflation.
comments.textZhHtml: 收缩通货膨胀已经结束。 20年前，快餐店的汉堡面包更加密集。小汉堡有 1/8 磅的肉饼，而不是现在的 1/10 磅。很难找到一种产品不会变得更糟或更贵，即使是根据通货膨胀进行调整。

children.author: xp84
children.textRawHtml: The burger patties were absolutely not 1/8 pound. I can assure you from experience as a Professional McDonald's Worker in 2003 that those were 10:1 patties then as well. I can also vouch for the same from another major burger chain circa 2001. I'm sure they shrink everything possible, but interestingly they haven't been shaving down the beef quantities for some reason.
children.textZhHtml: 汉堡肉饼绝对不是 1/8 磅。根据 2003 年作为一名专业麦当劳员工的经验，我可以向您保证，当时的肉饼比例也是 10:1。我也可以从 2001 年左右的另一家大型汉堡连锁店那里得到同样的保证。我确信他们尽可能缩小了尺寸，但有趣的是，出于某种原因，他们并没有减少牛肉的数量。

children.author: cestith
children.textRawHtml:
I worked at McDonald’s a decade prior to that, and they were 10:1 then, too. I think it’s possible and maybe likely some other chains might have switched from being 8:1 to 10:1 since the market leaders already had that size. There are much better examples though than some isolated regional player’s beef patty sizes.

We used to buy half gallons and gallons of ice cream. Brands started selling 60 or 62 ounces instead of 64. Over the years, it’s gotten to where some brands sell 48 ounces - three pints - instead of 64.

Breakfast cereals have had similar shrinking sizes.
children.textZhHtml:
十年前我在麦当劳工作，当时他们的比例也是 10:1。我认为这是可能的，也许其他一些连锁店可能已经从 8:1 转变为 10:1，因为市场领导者已经达到了这个规模。不过，有比一些孤立的区域参与者的牛肉饼尺寸更好的例子。

我们过去常常购买半加仑和加仑的冰淇淋。品牌开始销售 60 或 62 盎司，而不是 64 盎司。多年来，一些品牌的销售量已从 64 盎司（3 品脱）变为 48 盎司（3 品脱）。

早餐麦片的尺寸也有类似的缩小。

children.author: xp84
children.textRawHtml: Shrinkflation is to me the best example of why pure short-term-ism is a cancer. The first jackass to do it, say by taking a soup can of 16 ounces and adjusting it to 15.75oz, it boosted the profits that quarter. Mathematically, we could keep asymptotically shaving the size by 1.6% every couple years forever, but IRL that won't work because the amounts needed to be shaved would get so small as to not have the cost savings effect (or even be possible to precisely measure). So in reality the amounts need to be more like an actual quarter or half ounce at a time. So at some point the soup can, the candy bar, etc. would become so small that with one more shrink, people will recognize that it can't even feed one person, and at that point, all the "value" that was extracted by the previous CEOs to goose their stock price short term will be exhausted, and they'll have to move on to watering it down or whatever. But our packages will stay that idiotic minimum size forever.
children.textZhHtml: 对我来说，紧缩通货膨胀是解释为什么纯粹的短期主义是癌症的最好例子。第一个这么做的傻瓜，比如把一罐 16 盎司的汤罐头调整到 15.75 盎司，它提高了该季度的利润。从数学上讲，我们可以永远每几年渐近地削减 1.6%，但现实中这是行不通的，因为需要削减的数量会变得非常小，以至于无法产生成本节省效果（甚至无法精确测量）。因此，实际上，每次的数量需要更像是四分之一或半盎司。因此，到了某个时候，汤罐头、糖果棒等会变得如此之小，以至于再多一个心理医生，人们就会意识到它甚至无法养活一个人，到那时，前任首席执行官为短期内推高股价而提取的所有“价值”都将耗尽，他们将不得不继续淡化它或采取其他措施。但我们的包裹将永远保持那个愚蠢的最小尺寸。

children.author: cheschire
children.textRawHtml:
Don't you remember how they recovered from this after 2008? That's when they started selling "family size" options that are bigger, but with a not-so-obvious price increase where you can't really tell if it's more or less expensive per oz.

Price-conscious shoppers still buy the smaller thing if it's cheaper per oz (and only if the stores show the price per oz on the shelf), but most people just get the bigger size because that's how much they want to consume, and they can't really tell that the 15% increase in size does not equate to 19% increase in cost.

Many stores would stock the family size separate from the regular size so the shoppers couldnt easily compare price per oz.

Eventually the family size just becomes the regular size, but now at the higher price. Then the shrinking happens again.
children.textZhHtml:
您不记得 2008 年之后他们是如何恢复过来的吗？就在那时，他们开始销售更大的“家庭装”选项，但价格上涨不那么明显，你无法真正判断每盎司是否更贵。

如果每盎司更便宜，价格敏感的购物者仍然会购买较小的产品（并且只有当商店在货架上显示每盎司的价格时），但大多数人只是购买更大的尺寸，因为这就是他们想要消费的量，而且他们无法真正分辨出 15%尺寸增加并不等于成本增加 19%。

许多商店会将家庭尺寸与常规尺寸分开库存，因此购物者无法轻松比较每盎司的价格。

最终家庭尺寸只是变成常规尺寸，但现在价格更高。然后收缩再次发生。

children.author: noir_lord
children.textRawHtml:
> (and only if the stores show the price per oz on the shelf)

Legal requirement that they do in the UK (though in metric units), so it's £/L and £/Kg (or for smaller items per 100g and then some nuance on unit prices for things not sold by weight/volume).

It does make their shenanigans with multipacks and such way more obvious by design.

> The PMO also requires traders, where applicable, to display the ‘unit price’ – which is the price which would be charged for the relevant unit of the goods, depending upon how the goods are sold. Unit pricing can be a useful tool for consumers. It allows consumers to compare the price and value of similar products. This can be helpful when making a decision between similar products that are sold in different sizes or quantities.

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/price-marking-ord...
children.textZhHtml:
>（并且仅当商店在货架上显示每盎司的价格时）

他们在英国执行的法律要求（尽管以公制单位），因此它是 £/L 和 £/Kg（或对于每 100 克的较小物品，然后是不按重量/体积出售的物品的单价上的一些细微差别）。

这确实使他们在多件装上的恶作剧等等更多显而易见由设计。

> PMO还要求贸易商在适用的情况下显示“单价”——这是对相关商品单位收取的价格，具体取决于商品的销售方式。单价对于消费者来说是一个有用的工具。它允许消费者比较类似产品的价格和价值。在以不同尺寸或数量出售的类似产品之间做出决定时，这会很有帮助。

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/price-marking-ord...

children.author: account42
children.textRawHtml: And the same happens with subpar ingredients - when people notice they then bring back an "original formula" edition that is of course higher priced.
children.textZhHtml: 同样的情况也发生在低于标准的成分上 - 当人们注意到时，他们会带回“原始配方”版本，当然价格更高。

children.author: jimmydddd
children.textRawHtml: Many have noticed that the super large sizes at Costco, etc. often are more expensive per item or oz. than the sale price of a regular size at a Shoprite or whatever.
children.textZhHtml: 许多人注意到 Costco 等处的超大尺寸产品通常每件或每盎司的价格更高。比 Shoprite 或其他地方的常规尺寸的销售价格。

children.author: pjc50
children.textRawHtml: This is very old, though. The Roman era experienced monetary inflation through "coin clipping", which was literally shaving bits of silver off coins and remelting it together. This is why modern era coins often have milled tamper-evident edges, even if the metal is no longer worth the face value.
children.textZhHtml: 不过，这已经很古老了。罗马时代通过“剪币”经历了货币通货膨胀，这实际上是从硬币上削下银片并将其重新熔化在一起。这就是为什么现代硬币通常具有经过铣削的防篡改边缘，即使金属不再值面值。

children.author: furytrader
children.textRawHtml: Breakfast cereal boxes have gotten so small, it's ridiculous.  They might as well label the package "Fun Size" since it's clearly not "Full Size".
children.textZhHtml: 早餐麦片盒变得如此之小，这太荒谬了。  他们也可能在包装上贴上“有趣尺寸”的标签，因为它显然不是“全尺寸”。

children.author: therealdrag0
children.textRawHtml: Didn’t they also have filler then remove it to be 100% beef at some point?
children.textZhHtml: 他们不是也有填充物，然后在某个时候将其去除，成为 100% 牛肉吗？

children.author: x______________
children.textRawHtml:
100% beef is the topic of an ongoing lawsuit[0].

0 https://lawsips.com/mcdonalds-100-beef-lawsuit/
children.textZhHtml:
100% 牛肉是正在进行的诉讼的主题[0]。

0 https://lawsips.com/mcdonalds-100-beef-lawsuit/

children.author: johnwalkr
children.textRawHtml:
I was surprised to see a real reference because I thought the 100% beef thing was a 100% myth.

But that article confirms in several places that independent testing finds no fillers at all, and what is left is just "Plaintiffs allege that undisclosed processing steps or agents applied during production or cooking could alter the accuracy of the “100%” claim." It's not a very convincing argument and it would be quite hard for McDonalds to cover up a secret process to add another ingredient.
children.textZhHtml:
我很惊讶地看到了真实的参考资料，因为我认为 100% 牛肉的说法是 100% 的神话。

但那篇文章在几个地方证实了独立测试根本没有发现任何填充物，剩下的只是“原告声称在生产或烹饪过程中使用的未公开的加工步骤或试剂可能会改变“100%”声明的准确性。”这不是一个很有说服力的论点，麦当劳很难掩盖添加另一种成分的秘密过程。

children.author: lcnPylGDnU4H9OF
children.textRawHtml:
> Additionally, the visual gap between advertised burgers and actual burgers raises separate false advertising issues

Meanwhile, the very clear and obvious false advertising they actually perform is getting hardly any attention. Here's to hoping they won't be able to continue advertising products that are different from what they sell.
children.textZhHtml:
> 此外，广告中的汉堡和实际汉堡之间的视觉差距引发了单独的虚假广告问题

与此同时，他们实际执行的非常清晰和明显的虚假广告几乎没有引起任何关注。希望他们不能继续为与他们销售的产品不同的产品做广告。

children.author: FireBeyond
children.textRawHtml: Only after attempts to call one of their suppliers or processors "100% Beef" failed.
children.textZhHtml: 仅在尝试称其供应商或加工商之一为“100% 牛肉”失败后。

children.author: hydrogen7800
children.textRawHtml:
I recall a similar claim regarding pop music compilation CDs advertised as being performed by "The Original Cast", which was really a group by that name playing covers of popular songs.

Or another being "Made in USA", where Usa was a city in Korea.
children.textZhHtml:
我记得关于流行音乐合辑 CD 的类似说法，广告中声称是由“The Original Cast”演唱的，这实际上是一个以该名字命名的乐队，翻唱流行歌曲。

或者另一个是“美国制造”，其中美国是韩国的一座城市。

children.author: b112
children.textRawHtml:
"Genuine diamonds" sold fake diamonds after trademarking the name, I thibk. However a decade later I read about them losibg a lawsuit.

This tricks don't work any more.
children.textZhHtml:
“真钻石”在注册了该名称的商标后出售了假钻石，我想。 然而十年后，我读到有关他们败诉的消息。

这个伎俩不再起作用了。

children.author: tancop
children.textRawHtml:
the tricks never worked legally speaking. misleading labels stay misleading even if you have a trademark on that name and use it for years.

the problem is cases like this rarely go to court, and plaintiffs might run into a judge who literally doesnt believe consumer fraud is a thing if theres at least one possible non fraud interpretation no matter how unlikely it is.
children.textZhHtml:
从法律上讲，这些伎俩从来没有奏效。即使您在该名称上拥有商标并使用多年，误导性标签仍然具有误导性。

问题是这样的案件很少上法庭，而且如果至少有一种可能的非欺诈解释，无论可能性有多大，原告可能会遇到一位法官，他实际上并不相信消费者欺诈是一件事。

children.author: FireBeyond
children.textRawHtml:
I feel like there is a probably apocryphal story of a town in Japan being called Scotland so they can sell whisky as Scotch.

Which as a highlander I don’t see the need for - Japanese whiskey is quite able to stand in its own and hold its own.
children.textZhHtml:
我觉得有一个可能是杜撰的故事，日本的一个小镇被称为苏格兰，因此他们可以将威士忌称为苏格兰威士忌。

作为一个高地人，我认为没有必要 - 日本威士忌完全能够独立并保持自己的地位。
